transcript: Last night, I saw The Counter at Roundabout’s off-broadway house. At a tight 75 minutes, this new play by Meghan Kennedy directed by David Cromer is mostly a two hander of a waitress at a small cafe and one of her regular customers. It’s a quiet portrait of languishing and a search for meaning after profound losses. It wasn't the most original concept, as one of the major plot points was very reminiscent of another David Cromer directed play that I saw on Broadway in 2019. But the acting here was really great and the direction was consistent and natural. The writing was also realistic and funny, and the whole production had this very genuine bittersweet quality that really worked for me. One thing I'm skeptical about is the sight lines, which I feel like from some vantage points could be really bad. I was sitting house right and had a great profile view of the actors conversing over the counter, but because of the way the set is angled, I can't really imagine having a very good view from house left, so just keep that in mind. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
